**Case Study: Network Traffic Analysis Using Matrix Multiplication and Transpose**

A network administrator models data transferred (in GB) among three servers S1, S2, S3 over a week using this matrix:
$D=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 20 & 15 \\ 18 & 0 & 16 \\ 12 & 10 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$

Diagonal entries represent zero self-transfer. Another matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & a & b \\ c & 0 & d \\ e & f & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ models an attack traffic pattern. The admin analyzes symmetric and skew-symmetric parts of $A$.

(a) Express $A$ as the sum of its symmetric and skew-symmetric parts.

(b) For $a=20, b=15, c=18, d=16, e=12, f=10$, write $A$ and calculate $A'$ (transpose).

(c) Check if $A$ is symmetric or skew-symmetric and discuss the significance of each in the context of network security evaluation.
explanation:
(a)

Recall: Any square matrix $A$ can be written as $ rac{1}{2}(A+A') + rac{1}{2}(A-A')$.

Symmetric part: $S= rac{1}{2}(A+A')$

Skew-symmetric part: $K= rac{1}{2}(A-A')$.

(b)

Given $a=20, b=15, c=18, d=16, e=12, f=10$,

$A= egin{bmatrix} 0 & 20 & 15 \ 18 & 0 & 16 \ 12 & 10 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$

$A'= egin{bmatrix} 0 & 18 & 12 \ 20 & 0 & 10 \ 15 & 16 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$.

(c)

A is symmetric if $A=A'$, skew-symmetric if $A=-A'$.

Comparing $A$ and $A'$:

First: $20 eq18, 15 eq12, 16 eq10$, so $A eq A'$, also $A eq -A'$. So $A$ is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric.

In context: A symmetric matrix would indicate reciprocal (equal) traffic between server pairs, while skew-symmetric entries would mean one-way dominance (differential attack patterns). The analysis helps identify anomalies and assess security by separating regular (symmetric) from suspicious/asymmetric traffic.

options.B:
(a) $A=\frac12(A+A')+\frac12(A-A')$, where $\frac12(A+A')$ is symmetric and $\frac12(A-A')$ is skew-symmetric.
(b) $A=\begin{bmatrix}0&20&15\\18&0&16\\12&10&0\end{bmatrix}$ and $A'=\begin{bmatrix}0&18&12\\20&0&10\\15&16&0\end{bmatrix}$.
(c) $A$ is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric; symmetry would mean reciprocal traffic, while skew-symmetry would represent directional imbalance.
options.D:
(a) No decomposition exists for a $3\times3$ matrix.
(b) The transpose is not defined.
(c) Symmetry cannot be discussed for network matrices.
